Brian Kinstlinger: Okay. And then can you speak at a high level to SEALMINER and how you're thinking about production and capital allocation going forward?

Michael Potter: Jihan or Haris, do you want to talk about our SEALMINER?

Jihan Wu: Yeah. We will continue to invest into the expansion of our mining operations. I think next year we will slow down a little bit on the pace of investing new capital, but we will continue to expand our mining operations.

Operator: Our next question comes from Stephen Glagola with KBW.

Stephen Glagola: Haris and Michael, at Rockdale, can you clarify what infrastructure and related rights were transferred to Bitdeer as part of the $100 million transaction for the 200 acres? And specifically, did the purchase include SLR's interconnection rights and water rights and the SLR-owned substation?

Michael Potter: So it didn't include the water rights, but we do have an arrangement to get water to the site as part of the deal, but the water rights themselves were not transferred over. In terms of power, we have control over the interconnection now and the ability to transfer power from our existing site to the new site.

Stephen Glagola: Okay. Great. And did you guys purchase the substation as well?

Michael Potter: We have an agreement to share the substation because the SLR does use a small part of the substation that we mainly use. So it's more formal and with us more in control versus them being in control as our landlord.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our next question comes from Kevin Dede with JonesTrading.

Unknown Analyst: Kind of curious about how you see Malaysia developing. I know that it's been a big focus for your AI cloud business, and I'm wondering if you see Bitdeer in an advantageous position in competing for, I think what you said is underserved AI startups in that region versus other competitors perhaps, and maybe offer a little comparison with how you see that business evolving in the U.S.

Jihan Wu: I think it's quite good for us to be able to expand in Malaysia, especially in this kind of midterm uncertainty in U.S. We will be able to expand our AI cloud business on time without to worry about our own data center construction pace. And right now, most of the U.S. companies, Asian-based tech companies are all looking to Malaysia capacity. Our U.S. sales team get lots of inbound demand inquiries about our capacity in Malaysia. Because right now it's really hard to rent any data centers in United States within next year, RFS.

So I think it's really great that we can lock lots of capacity in Malaysia and continue to lock more and grow the AI cloud there. And while at the same time, our U.S. data centers are being built in DeepLab on the U.S. speed. So we don't need to really worry about whether our AI cloud can grow or not. We can just execute and fulfill the demand from our customers.

Unknown Analyst: I am also curious about wafer allocation from TSMC and your, I guess, your plan to use it. I know last quarter you mentioned Scrypt mining, and I am wondering how you are looking at Zcash and the wafer availability itself and associated pricing.

Jihan Wu: I think our wafer availability is a little bit tight, much tighter than before because of the strong demand from AI. So I think we will slow a little bit on the CapEx on crypto mining business next year. And we have no plan for doing Zcash. And Scrypt mining right now is really good for us because in terms of revenue dollar per megawatt, it's higher than Bitcoin mining, and we will have an edge over other competitors in terms of the mining machines in this algorithm. So we will continue to do more Scrypt mining.

Unknown Analyst: The feedback I have gotten is that Zcash is incredibly profitable and there is very huge shortage of machines given that there only seems to be one manufacturer who you know well.

Jihan Wu: Yeah. But the competition for the Zcash mining, I think, will also be very fierce. Lots of potential new Zcash mining rig developers are already in the market to take out and to order lots of wafers from Samsung and TSMC. So I think to strategically give up Zcash is good for us.

Operator: Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Potter for any closing remarks.

Michael Potter: Thanks, everybody, for joining our call today, and I look forward to talking to you in the future. Thank you.

Operator: This concludes the conference. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Marvell Stock’s Selloff Is Overdone as Solid Upside and Valuation Reset Revives Investment Appeal
news.Content:
Marvell Technology's (MRVL) stock has corrected sharply, falling about 44% over the past month and trading about 54% below its 52-week high. The sharp decline reflects multiple concerns surrounding the company's proposed acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (LITE), broader weakness across AI-related equities, and growing investor scrutiny of the economics of large-scale AI infrastructure investments.

In early November 2026, Marvell announced an agreement to acquire Lumentum, a manufacturer of optical components and lasers, through an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115 billion. Under the proposed terms, Marvell will issue 4.5 new shares for each Lumentum share. This would significantly increase Marvell's outstanding share count, with existing Marvell shareholders retaining about 67% ownership of the combined entity.

More News from Barchart

Nvidia Stock Could Shed Up to $225 Billion Over Jensen Huang Probe, But Rival AMD's Rally Shows It's Not an AI Demand Problem

CEO Lip-Bu Tan's 150,000-Share Purchase Wasn't Enough to Stop the Slide in Intel Stock

Dear D-Wave Quantum Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

The transaction's substantial equity component has emerged as a key source of investor concern. The anticipated dilution has raised questions about the acquisition's impact on per-share earnings, shareholder returns, and overall capital efficiency.

Moreover, Marvell's decline has also occurred against a broader deterioration in sentiment toward artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks. Investors are questioning the long-term return on investment from the enormous capital commitments technology companies are making toward AI data centers. Concerns about the sustainability of infrastructure spending, the monetization of AI services, and potential regulatory or policy restrictions on data center development have added to near-term market uncertainty.

Nevertheless, the notable decline in Marvell's stock has made its risk-reward profile more compelling. While acquisition-related dilution and integration risks warrant caution, the selloff has also lowered MRVL's valuation. This presents an attractive entry point, as Marvell is well-positioned to capitalize on demand for AI infrastructure and optical connectivity solutions.

In addition, analysts see substantial upside in MRVL stock, strengthening its investment case.

Marvell's Growth Prospects Remain Solid

Story Continues

Marvell appears well-positioned to deliver strong growth through the end of the decade, supported by solid AI-driven demand and its expanding addressable market following the proposed acquisition.

The semiconductor company earlier raised its growth guidance and said that its revenue would hit $20 billion in fiscal 2028. The outlook represented a $2 billion increase from its previous target and approximately 67% year-over-year (YoY) growth. Looking further ahead, Marvell projected its revenue will expand at a CAGR of 55% to 60% through fiscal 2031.

Rising demand for AI accelerators, high-speed connectivity, networking solutions, and custom silicon is creating multiple opportunities for Marvell to expand its market presence. Management expects data center revenue to grow at a CAGR of approximately 65% between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2031.

In addition, the proposed all-stock acquisition of Lumentum could further strengthen Marvell's long-term growth prospects despite concerns around shareholder dilution and integration risk. The deal is expected to expand the company's addressable market to $550 billion by calendar year 2030. By combining their technology platforms, Marvell and Lumentum could address a broader range of AI infrastructure needs, particularly in optical connectivity. This would give the combined company more opportunities to compete for a larger share of the growing market. Management also expects the acquisition to be accretive from the first year, with initial synergies and the potential for additional cost savings over time.

Strong revenue growth will translate into solid earnings. Marvell's growing custom silicon business and improved operating efficiency are expected to support higher profitability over time. Management believes EPS could exceed $30 by fiscal 2031, suggesting considerable long-term earnings growth potential.

In the near term, analysts expect fiscal 2028 EPS to reach $6.08, up 99.3%, supporting its investment case.

Valuation Reset Makes MRVL Stock More Compelling

While shareholder dilution, integration challenges, and uncertainty surrounding AI infrastructure spending remain key risks, much of the near-term pessimism appears reflected in MRVL stock. Further, Marvell's sharp correction appears overdone relative to its long-term growth potential, creating a more attractive valuation.

Strong AI-driven demand, expanding opportunities in custom silicon and optical connectivity, and the potential strategic benefits of the Lumentum acquisition support the company's long-term growth outlook.

Moreover, analysts are bullish and maintain a "Strong Buy" consensus rating. At 43.9 times forward earnings, Marvell's valuation appears reasonable relative to its growth potential. Furthermore, the average analyst price target of $308.40 suggests about 99% upside over the next 12 months from its Nov. 9 closing price of $154.60.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold Cisco Systems Stock Before Q1 Earnings?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO is set to release its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco Systems expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be in the range of $1.32-$1.34 per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues is pegged at $18.09 billion, suggesting 21.54% year-over-year growth. The consensus mark for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $1.33 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days and indicates 33% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

CSCO's earnings surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, the average being 2.55%.

Cisco Systems, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Cisco Systems, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Cisco Systems, Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Key Factors to Note for CSCO's Q1 Earnings

Cisco Systems' fiscal first-quarter 2027 performance is expected to have benefited from strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, growing hyperscaler investments and continued enterprise network modernization. Increasing adoption of agentic AI is driving demand for high-performance networking solutions across cloud, on-premises and edge environments. Cisco Systems' expanding portfolio of networking, security and observability solutions is expected to have supported revenue growth in the to-be-reported quarter.

AI infrastructure spending by hyperscalers is expected to have remained a major growth driver. Cisco Systems secured $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, bringing full-year orders to $9.3 billion. Growing adoption of Silicon One-based systems, Acacia optics and high-performance networking solutions is likely to have supported revenues. The company's expanding design wins with hyperscalers remain noteworthy.

Enterprise networking demand is expected to have strengthened Cisco Systems' performance. Increasing investments in data center modernization, campus networking and AI-ready infrastructure are likely to have driven demand for switching, routing and wireless solutions. Data center networking orders increased by more than 35% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while campus networking orders grew 20%. Strong adoption of Wi-Fi 7 and next-generation switches is expected to have sustained this momentum.

Cisco Systems' security business is expected to have benefited from increasing cybersecurity spending and growing adoption of its integrated security offerings. Rising demand for Secure Access, XDR, Hypershield, AI Defense and firewall solutions is likely to have supported growth. Strengthening Splunk adoption and integration with Cisco Systems' broader security portfolio are additional positives. Management anticipates mid-to-high-single-digit security revenue growth in the to-be-reported quarter.

However, Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 performance is expected to have faced pressure from rising memory costs and a higher mix of lower-margin hardware revenues, potentially weighing on gross margins. The company is also suffering from stiff competition from Arista Networks ANET, Dell Technologies DELL and Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE across AI networking and enterprise security domains.

Story Continues

CSCO Shares Outperform Sector

Cisco Systems' shares have appreciated 28.1% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 4.1%.

However, CSCO's shares have underperformed Arista Networks, Dell Technologies and Hewlett-Packard Enterprise YTD. Shares of Dell Technologies, Arista Networks and Hewlett-Packard have appreciated 175.1%, 42.1% and 98%, respectively.

CSCO Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation for Cisco at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, CSCO is trading at 5.3X, higher than the broader sector's 4.84X, Dell Technologies' 0.99X and Hewlett Packard Enterprise's 1.15X, but lower than Arista Networks' 13.43X.

CSCO Valuation

Cisco Rides on Strong Portfolio & AI Demand

Cisco Systems' long-term prospects remain promising, driven by its diversified networking, security, observability and collaboration portfolio, alongside rising investments in AI infrastructure.

Strong AI infrastructure demand remains a key growth catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027, supported by growing demand and market share gains. Increasing adoption of its Silicon One P200 and G200 systems, alongside expanding opportunities in scale-out and scale-across networking, should further strengthen its growth trajectory.

Cisco Systems' security and observability businesses offer substantial growth opportunities as enterprises increasingly prioritize protection against AI-related cyber threats. The integration of Splunk with Cisco Systems security portfolio, alongside growing adoption of Hypershield, AI Defense and Secure Access, should support cross-selling opportunities and recurring revenue growth. Management expects security and observability revenues to grow at a high-single-digit rate in fiscal 2027.

Conclusion

Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 results are likely to reflect strong AI infrastructure momentum, robust networking demand and an expanding security portfolio. Rising hyperscaler investments, growing adoption of Silicon One and improving Splunk momentum further strengthen its growth prospects. These factors justify its premium valuation.

CSCO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: APPS Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Ad Growth, Guidance Up
news.Content:
Digital Turbine APPS reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, up 20% from 15 cents in the year-ago quarter. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 12.5%.

Net revenues totaled $178.68 million, increasing 27.3% year over year and surpassing the consensus estimate by 7.24%. Strength across the On Device Solutions and App Growth Platform segments, supported by AI-driven advertising improvements, fueled growth. Adjusted EBITDA increased 46% year over year.

APPS' Q2 Revenue Growth Drivers

Digital Turbine's On Device Solutions segment generated $115.6 million in net revenues before intercompany eliminations, up 20% year over year. International revenues grew approximately 50%, supported by higher device volumes and improved revenue per device despite smartphone supply-chain headwinds.

App Growth Platform revenues reached $63.5 million, increasing 42% year over year. This marked the segment's fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and third consecutive quarter of more than 40% growth. DT Exchange revenues increased 42%, while the brand business grew 45%, reflecting stronger advertiser demand and AI-powered optimization.

Digital Turbine, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Digital Turbine, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Digital Turbine, Inc. Quote

Digital Turbine's AI Initiatives Gain Traction

Management highlighted improving advertising performance through its first-party data and AI-powered targeting capabilities. Higher advertiser returns on ad spending supported stronger pricing and fill rates, particularly across premium advertising placements.

The company also benefited from increasing demand for mobile-app advertising and diversification beyond gaming. Nearly 40% of advertiser spending on DT Exchange came from non-gaming partners. Digital Turbine continues expanding its publisher network, particularly across Asia Pacific, while attracting AI-focused applications seeking monetization opportunities.

APPS' Q2 Operating Details

The non-GAAP gross margin contracted 400 basis points (bps) year over year to 43%.

Sales and marketing expenses, as a percentage of revenues, declined to 8.1% from 10.3% in the year-ago quarter. General and administrative expenses decreased to 18.3% of revenues from 24.3%, while product development expenses declined to 5.6% from 7.8%.

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased to $39.8 million from $27.2 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded approximately 290 bps to 22.3%, reflecting improved operating leverage and expense discipline.

Digital Turbine reported GAAP operating income of $20.3 million compared with $6.5 million in the year-ago quarter. GAAP net income reached $10.3 million against a net loss of $21.4 million a year earlier.

Story Continues

Digital Turbine's Cash Flow and Balance Sheet

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $51.62 million compared with $43.21 million at the end of the preceding quarter.

Cash flow from operating activities was $18.84 million compared with $14.46 million in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP free cash flow increased to $10.46 million from $7.03 million, reflecting improved cash generation despite continued investments in the business.

Total debt, net of issuance costs and discounts, stood at approximately $353.61 million. Management highlighted continued deleveraging, with the net leverage ratio improving to approximately 2.3 times from more than 4 times a year earlier.

APPS Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue Guidance

For fiscal 2027, Digital Turbine now expects revenues between $670 million and $690 million, up from the previously guided range of $650 million to $670 million. The company reaffirmed its adjusted EBITDA guidance of $145 million to $155 million.

Management attributed the improved revenue outlook to sustained momentum in AI-driven advertising, stronger performance across its platforms and increased partner adoption. The company plans additional investments in data science, machine learning and AI infrastructure during the second half of fiscal 2027 to support future growth.

Digital Turbine's Expanding Global Opportunities

International expansion remains a key priority. Management expects initial revenues from its Orange partnership in the current quarter and anticipates launching services with another Tier 1 European telecommunications operator during fiscal 2027. These partnerships are expected to contribute more meaningfully to growth in fiscal 2028.

Digital Turbine is also expanding its Ignite platform beyond traditional app distribution into AI agents, e-commerce, lock-screen services and other content offerings. Management expects its expanding device footprint and AI-enabled advertising capabilities to support continued revenue growth, while incremental investments could moderate near-term profitability gains.

APPS's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Digital Turbine currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector include Cisco Systems CSCO, Analog Devices ADI and NVIDIA NVDA. Each stock presently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Cisco Systems shares have gained 28.1% year to date. Cisco Systems is set to report first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

Shares of Analog Devices have risen 45.5% year to date. Analog Devices is set to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 24.

NVIDIA shares have lost 4.2% year to date. NVIDIA is set to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17.

news.Title: 5 AI Stock Picks and Performance of Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller
news.Content:
Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller has been bullish on AI since before ChatGPT launched. He is one of the most closely followed macro investors on Wall Street. He averaged about 30% a year at Duquesne Capital with no losing year, and his 1992 bet against the British pound made more than $1 billion.

Druckenmiller's AI Stock Picks Take a Beating

The AI trade has taken a turn for the worse since the end of the second quarter. Nine of Stanley Druckenmiller's 10 AI stock picks on this list have declined since June 30, with the stocks losing an average of 27.8% on an equal-weight basis through November 9, compared with a gain of about 0.8% for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). We have included each stock's performance since June 30 in the list below. But did Druckenmiller get out before the crash? We could find out in just a few days, when his family office is expected to disclose its third-quarter holdings. The filing will reveal whether he sold or reduced positions before the latest AI selloff, or held on to stocks that subsequently suffered steep losses.

To find out what Druckenmiller bought and sold, follow Stanley Druckenmiller's page on our website and sign up for email notifications.

Why He Bought Nvidia Before the AI Boom

Druckenmiller told CNBC in May 2024 that his young partner urged him in 2022 to buy Nvidia. He bought it, and a month later ChatGPT launched, so he raised the position substantially. He cut the stake in late March 2024 after a huge run, and he said he is not Warren Buffett and does not hold stocks for 20 years. He called AI a little over-hyped in the short term and under-hyped in the long term.

Speaking of Buffett, we ranked the Berkshire Hathaway holdings with the most room to rise in our list of the 10 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential .

Is AI a Bubble? What Druckenmiller Has Said

Druckenmiller has called AI real from the start. In a June 2023 Bloomberg interview, he said AI is real, unlike crypto. He said real secular shifts do not move in 10 months, and that the internet bubble lasted about two and a half years. He wanted to own Nvidia for at least two to three years.

By May 2024, his tone had changed. He told CNBC that AI could be a little over-hyped now and under-hyped in the long term. He compared it to the internet in 1999, when someone who bought the Nasdaq watched it fall 80% before the internet's payoff arrived. What He Says About AI, Jobs and Inflation

news.Title: What Bitdeer Technologies Group (BTDR) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Bitdeer Technologies Group? Here are five stocks we like better.

Revenue reached a record $320.7 million , up 89% year over year, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $69.6 million. Bitdeer still reported a $125.5 million net loss amid heavy investment.

Management cited about $7.6 billion in expected contracted AI revenue and 332 IT megawatts of secured data-center capacity. AI cloud revenue grew 46% sequentially to $20.4 million, while construction and customer installations at key sites are scheduled to ramp from late 2026 into 2027.

Spending sharply reduced cash to $163.7 million from $456.8 million as quarterly capital expenditures reached $478 million and debt rose to $1.95 billion. Bitdeer is pursuing project and asset-level financing, while lowering its 2026 crypto-mining infrastructure capex outlook to $200 million or less.

4 Blockchain Stocks That Aren't Coinbase

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR) reported record third-quarter revenue as Bitcoin production and co-mining expanded, while management outlined plans to finance a growing pipeline of artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.

Revenue rose 89% year over year to $320.7 million, and adjusted EBITDA increased to $69.6 million from $25.5 million a year earlier. The company posted a net loss of $125.5 million, or $0.46 per share, as it invested heavily in data centers and computing equipment.

→ The Ugly Truth Behind SoundHound's Q3 Results

Beyond the Halving: The Future of Bitcoin Mining Stocks

Chief Strategy Officer Haris Basit said Bitdeer's AI platform represents approximately $7.6 billion in expected contracted revenue: about $4.7 billion from the base term of its Tydal data center lease in Norway and $2.9 billion in AI cloud backlog. The two businesses have different revenue recognition profiles and capital requirements, he said.

AI Cloud Contracts and Tydal Construction

AI cloud revenue increased 46% from the second quarter to $20.4 million. Bitdeer ended September with 4,328 graphics processing units deployed at approximately 95% utilization. The business generated $3.1 million in gross profit, compared with a $2.3 million gross loss in the prior quarter.

→ Lemonade's Revenue Soars 73%—So Why Did Its Stock Turn Sour After Earnings?

Chief Financial Officer Michael Potter said the sequential revenue increase came primarily from pricing and customer mix as utilization of higher-value systems rose. AI cloud annualized recurring revenue was approximately $86 million at quarter-end.

Story Continues

In Malaysia, Bitdeer has sold out the 9.5 megawatts of capacity at its A102 facility under five-year commitments representing more than $800 million in expected revenue. More than 70% of the 21.7 megawatts at A201 is contracted, representing over $1.7 billion in expected five-year revenue. The company expects revenue to begin at A102 in the first quarter of 2027 and at A201 in the second quarter.

→ Anthropic's S-1 Strengthens the Case for Broadcom's AI Growth

Potter said secured AI cloud data center capacity has reached approximately 332 IT megawatts, or about 95% of the company's target for the first quarter of 2028. He cautioned that secured capacity, which includes owned sites and those covered by executed data center services agreements, is not the same as capacity contracted to customers.

At Tydal, phase-one delivery remains scheduled for year-end, with customer installations planned to begin in January. Phase-two data hall deliveries are expected to start at the end of the first quarter of 2027. The lease with Volta covers 121 IT megawatts over 16 years, subject to the tenant's right to terminate without a fee after 10 years.

Potter said Bitdeer has begun the project-financing process. He also said Volta's reported GPU financing removed a major item needed to activate the anticipated letter-of-credit support, with construction completion and operational GPUs among the remaining steps.

Cash Declines as Spending Rises

Bitdeer ended the quarter with $163.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $456.8 million at the end of the second quarter. Capital expenditures totaled $478 million, including approximately $288 million for data center construction and land and about $110 million for SEALMINER production. Total debt rose to $1.95 billion.

Potter said cash declined because the company funded Tydal construction and a land purchase at Rockdale ahead of expected financing. Operating cash flow was approximately $6 million, including customer prepayments. The company also sold $221.5 million of mined Bitcoin, proceeds reported in investing activities.

Management expects customer prepayments and asset-level financing to support AI cloud deployments. Potter said financing for the A102 GPUs was in its final stages, while work was underway on a similar arrangement for A201. Deferred revenue, mostly AI cloud prepayments, reached approximately $342 million at quarter-end.

During the call, Potter gave differing figures for remaining Tydal construction spending, citing approximately $350 million and approximately $250 million in prepared remarks, then about $500 million during questions. He did not reconcile the figures. He said the company would seek at least $500 million in financing and hoped to recover some equity previously invested in the site, subject to market conditions.

Bitdeer raised $58 million through its at-the-market equity program in the third quarter, compared with $457 million in the second. Potter said the company had not recently accessed equity markets but declined to rule out future equity financing.

Mining Growth and Capital Outlook

Bitdeer mined 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter, up 43% from the second quarter, while co-mining revenue rose 140% sequentially to $59.9 million. Self-mining hash rate reached approximately 82.3 exahash per second at quarter-end.

Power cost per Bitcoin mined was approximately $36,000, down from $49,000 a year earlier, as fleet efficiency improved. Total gross profit was $10.8 million, reversing a second-quarter gross loss, although average power costs rose to 4.7 cents per kilowatt-hour from 4.4 cents.

The company now expects 2026 crypto mining infrastructure capital spending at or below $200 million, the low end of its previous $200 million to $280 million range. The forecast excludes SEALMINER hardware, GPUs, AI cloud and high-performance computing infrastructure. Potter said Bitdeer plans to provide 2027 guidance with its fourth-quarter results.

Founder and CEO Jihan Wu said Bitdeer expects to slow the pace of new crypto-mining capital investment next year while continuing to expand operations. At Rockdale, he said the company plans to seek additional grid power and build new AI data centers on acquired land rather than broadly winding down existing mining operations.

About Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR)

Bitdeer Technologies Group is a technology company focused on cryptocurrency mining and related infrastructure. Its business includes operating mining data centers, mining digital assets for its own account, and providing hosting services that allow customers to deploy and operate mining equipment.

The company also develops and sells cryptocurrency mining machines and offers cloud hash rate services, which provide customers access to computing capacity for mining without requiring them to operate the equipment themselves.

news.Title: ‘Baby Berkshire’ Portfolio: 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy According to Warren Buffett Disciple Tom Gayner
news.Content: The recent AI stock selloff has investors asking how long AI stocks will take to win back confidence. Many are looking at old-school billionaires and veteran money managers who have worked through several market cycles. One of the best-known is Tom Gayner, the CEO of Markel Group. Gayner is a staunch Warren Buffett follower, and Forbes titled its 2024 profile of him "Inside a Baby Berkshire Hathaway." This list shows the 10 biggest AI-related holdings in Markel's latest 13F filing. We also ranked the Berkshire holdings with the most upside in our list of the 10 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential . How Gayner Became a Buffett Student Gayner graduated from the University of Virginia in 1983 and later took a job at Davenport & Co., a stockbroker in Richmond, Virginia. Soon after, he read about Buffett and became deeply interested in his investing philosophy. In 1990, Gayner left Davenport to join Markel, an insurance-based holding company that the Markel family started in 1930. Markel also owns a large stock portfolio and a group of private businesses. Gayner ran the stock investments, and his first purchase was Berkshire Hathaway stock. He became co-CEO in 2016 and has been the sole CEO since 2023. Why Markel Is Called "Baby Berkshire" Markel uses the Berkshire model. It runs an insurance business, owns a large stock portfolio, and controls a group of private companies. Cash from Markel's profitable insurance business has flowed into Gayner's portfolio every month since 1990, the Wall Street Journal reported in 2015. Berkshire is also the cornerstone of Markel's portfolio. Its Class A and Class B shares made up 6.48% and 5.94% of Markel's reported portfolio at the end of September 2026. Gayner told Barron's that the friendships and network he built around Berkshire's meetings have no equal. See the Berkshire picks with the most upside in our list of the 5 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential . Has Gayner Beaten the Market? Jason Zweig, a Wall Street Journal columnist, wrote about Gayner's record in a 2015 column . Zweig also wrote the new commentary for the 2003 edition of Benjamin Graham's The Intelligent Investor , a book Buffett has called the best investing book ever written. Zweig reported that Gayner's stocks returned an average of 11.3% a year over the prior 15 years. The S&P 500 returned 4.2% a year with dividends in the same period. In 2008, Gayner's portfolio fell 34% and the S&P 500 fell 37%. Zweig also reported that Gayner ran the portfolio for less than 0.01% in annual expenses. Story Continues Tom Gayner of Markel Gayner Asset Management Methodology To compile our list of the 10 AI stocks Tom Gayner's Markel Group is holding, we examined Markel's third-quarter 2026 13F portfolio, which disclosed about $12.84 billion in holdings across 145 stocks as of September 30. We selected 10 holdings tied to AI. Alphabet's Class A and Class C shares count as one company. The stocks are ranked in ascending order of Markel's reported stake value as of September 30, 2026, with the largest holding at number one. Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ). #10 Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) Markel Stake as of Q3: $18.6 Million Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) makes the equipment chipmakers use to build semiconductors, so its sales rise when companies spend more on AI chip factories. Tom Gayner's Markel Group held 36,350 shares at the end of September 2026, which is 0.14% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Cambiar Opportunity Fund said in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter that AI compute expansion and memory shortages extend Applied Materials' growth runway, so see the Cambiar letter here . Applied Materials shares are down about 34% over the past month. The selloff started after the midterm elections, when investors began to worry that a Democratic Congress would make it harder to build new data centers. Fewer data centers would mean fewer new chip factories, and that hurts equipment makers first. Bulls say the fear is too big. Federal lawmakers can write rules, but state and local governments decide whether a data center gets built, and many of them depend on the property taxes and jobs these projects bring. Bulls also say that even a slower build-out still needs a steady flow of new chip factories, and a company that sells one of the widest ranges of chip-making equipment sits at the center of that spending. Applied Materials also holds more cash than debt, which gives it room to get through a slow stretch. #9 Comfort Systems USA, Inc. (NYSE:FIX) Markel Stake as of Q3: $21.5 Million Comfort Systems USA (NYSE:FIX) installs heating, cooling, and electrical systems in commercial buildings, and data centers are a growing part of its work. Markel held 13,000 shares at the end of September 2026, or 0.17% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Parnassus Investments said in its second-quarter 2026 letter for the Parnassus Growth Equity Fund that Comfort Systems is positioned to benefit from accelerated AI investment, so check the Parnassus letter here . Comfort Systems USA (NYSE:FIX) is one of the under-the-radar AI plays in Tom Gayner's portfolio. Data centers run hot, so every new one needs large cooling and power systems that a contractor has to install and maintain. Bulls say that work will keep coming because big tech companies plan to keep spending on data centers, and Comfort Systems also serves hospitals, schools, and factories. Bears point to the stock's drop of about 40% over the past three months, which followed fears that a Democratic Congress will slow new data center projects. A contractor's revenue falls quickly if projects get delayed. #8 Accenture plc (NYSE:ACN) Markel Stake as of Q3: $29.2 Million Accenture (NYSE:ACN) is a consulting and technology services company that helps big businesses build and run AI systems. Markel held 159,400 shares at the end of September 2026, which is 0.23% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Diamond Hill Capital said in its second-quarter 2026 letter for its Large Cap Strategy that Accenture could be an undervalued AI opportunity after its sharp selloff. See the Diamond Hill thesis here . Accenture is an AI play because companies need help putting AI to work, and Accenture gets paid to do it. More than 400 clients started their first advanced AI projects with Accenture in fiscal 2026. Bulls say the stock is still cheap. Investors feared AI would replace consultants, and those fears have faded. The shares trade at about 18 times forward earnings, below their 10-year average of about 26. The lower multiple comes with slower growth. Analysts expect Accenture's earnings per share to grow about 5% in fiscal 2027, in line with company guidance of 3% to 6%, and about 8% in fiscal 2028. Bears say AI can hurt Accenture as well as help it. Baird downgraded the stock after a near 100% gain since June, saying clients could use AI to work more efficiently and give Accenture less work. #7 Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) Markel Stake as of Q3: $38.3 Million Markel held 355,500 shares of Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) at the end of September 2026, which is 0.30% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. The London Company said in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter that strong AI infrastructure orders drive confidence in Cisco. See the full letter here . Morgan Stanley recently downgraded Cisco to equal-weight from overweight, and the reasons apply to the whole AI story. The shares rose 43% over the past 12 months, compared with 14% for the S&P 500. Morgan Stanley says a large part of the AI-driven gain is already in the price. Cisco trades at about 19 times forward earnings, a higher multiple than it has had in the past, so there is little room for the stock to beat what investors already expect. Morgan Stanley also pointed to lower gross margins from Cisco's AI business, and it was worried about the margins on the cloud business. It added that some customers may have bought early to get ahead of Cisco's price increases, which could mean weaker orders later. Morgan Stanley still likes the business itself. It sees several years of double-digit growth, mostly from cloud customers, and says that supports a higher multiple than Cisco has had before. #6 Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) Markel Stake as of Q3: $151.7 Million Markel held 209,163 shares of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) at the end of September 2026, or 1.18% of its reported portfolio. It trimmed the position by 10.68% in the quarter. Retail investors are debating whether Meta is dead money or the best cheap AI stock. Click to see both sides . Many readers will be surprised to see Meta in Tom Gayner's portfolio. The Wall Street Journal has reported that Gayner looks for profitable companies with good management and a reasonable stock price. Meta is now spending so much on AI data centers that its free cash flow turned negative in its most recent quarter. Bears say Meta's only real moat is its huge base of users, which lets it sell ads at high prices. They say AI models are becoming commodities, because many companies now sell similar ones, so Meta will struggle to earn much from its own. Muse, Meta's new AI model, is growing fast but is still small next to the cost of the data centers behind it. Meta also has no big cloud business to rent out its spare computing capacity, unlike Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet, the Journal reported. That means Meta has to earn back its AI spending through its own apps. Bulls point to those same apps. In the most recent quarter, Meta's average price per ad rose 14% and the number of ads shown rose 10% from the same quarter a year ago. The stock trades at about 21 times forward earnings, close to its own five-year average of about 22. Bulls say that is a fair price for a business that still grows ads this fast. news.Title: ASTS Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Higher Costs Offset Revenue Growth
news.Content:
AST SpaceMobile, Inc. ASTS reported lackluster third-quarter 2026 results, with both earnings and revenues missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. The company reported a loss of 44 cents per share, wider than the consensus estimate of a loss of 41 cents, representing a negative surprise of 7.3%. However, the loss narrowed from 45 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.

Quarterly revenues surged 187.1% year over year to $42.32 million but missed the consensus estimate of $44.47 million by 4.8%. Growth was driven by commercial gateway deliveries and U.S. government contract milestones. However, elevated operating expenses continued to pressure profitability.

ASTS Sees Robust Growth Across Revenue Streams

Product revenues increased 165.6% year over year to $20.57 million from $7.75 million in the prior-year quarter. Growth was primarily driven by commercial gateway equipment deliveries to mobile network operator partners as the company expanded its ground infrastructure.

Service revenues surged 211% to $21.75 million from $6.99 million a year ago. The increase reflected progress in U.S. government programs and the achievement of contractual milestones. The company continues to benefit from growing demand for its space-based communication and sensing capabilities.

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Quote

AST SpaceMobile's Operating Costs Remain Elevated

Total operating expenses increased 123.5% year over year to $211.03 million from $94.42 million. Engineering services costs surged 134.6% to $95.79 million, reflecting investments in satellite manufacturing, workforce expansion and network development.

General and administrative expenses increased 86.8% to $55.71 million. Research and development expenses rose to $9.09 million from $5.53 million. Depreciation and amortization expenses increased to $25.08 million from $12.72 million.

Adjusted operating expenses were $133.6 million, up from $119.1 million in the preceding quarter. Excluding adjusted cost of revenues, adjusted operating expenses totaled $109.4 million, within management's previously guided range of $105 million to $115 million.

ASTS Advances Satellite Manufacturing and Deployment

AST SpaceMobile accelerated its satellite manufacturing roadmap by advancing next-generation application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) integration to BlueBird 34 from the originally planned BlueBird 50. The upgraded technology is expected to deliver a 10-fold improvement in processing bandwidth compared with its existing Block 1 satellites.

The company is manufacturing satellites through BlueBird 51 at its Texas facilities. Two factories are operating full shifts, supporting management's target of producing six ASIC-enabled satellites monthly by December 2026.

Story Continues

BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 have been shipped to Cape Canaveral, while additional satellite shipments are planned through January 2027. Management targets approximately 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid-2027, with launch agreements covering more than 100 satellites for deployment during 2027 and 2028.

AST SpaceMobile Expands Commercial and Government Reach

The company expects to activate intermittent nationwide satellite broadband coverage in the United States and other key markets before the end of 2026. Initial rollout markets include Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom.

AST SpaceMobile has agreements with more than 60 mobile network operators representing over three billion subscribers globally. It also successfully validated satellite beam handovers between terrestrial and space-based cellular networks with AT&T, marking an important step toward commercial service deployment.

Government opportunities are expanding. The company secured an approximately $100 million U.S. Space Force contract for advanced space-based sensing capabilities. Capital expenditures totaled approximately $310 million during the third quarter, down from approximately $610 million in the preceding quarter. The lower spending primarily reflected timing-related shifts in launch payments.

The company also announced Blacklift, its planned reusable rocket capable of carrying up to five BlueBird satellites per launch. Initial launches are targeted for late 2028, potentially providing greater control over satellite deployment schedules.

AST SpaceMobile Reaffirms 2026 Revenue Outlook

Management reiterated its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150 million to $200 million, with potential upside from recently signed contracts. Revenue generation is expected to benefit from gateway deliveries, government contract milestones, consulting services and software licensing.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, AST SpaceMobile expects adjusted operating expenses, excluding adjusted cost of revenues, between $130 million and $140 million. Capital expenditures are projected between $400 million and $500 million, reflecting continued satellite production and launch-related investments.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold HPE Stock at a P/E Multiple of 10.08X?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 10.08X, below the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's P/E of 16.76X. The discounted valuation of HPE stock is further substantiated by the Zacks Value Score of A.

HPE Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The discounted valuation remains despite HPE stock climbing 98% year to date, outperforming the broader sector and the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry's return of 65.2% and 4.1%, respectively.

HPE YTD Performance Chart

HPE Experiences Growth Across Cloud and Networking

Hewlett Packard Enterprise operates across three primary business segments, namely Cloud & AI, Networking, and Corporate Investments and Other, serving enterprise customers with infrastructure, software, services and flexible consumption solutions. Cloud & AI combines HPE's server, storage and financial services businesses.

HPE's server portfolio includes general-purpose and workload-optimized systems, high-performance computing, supercomputing, AI infrastructure, data analytics and transaction processing. Its storage offerings include HPE Alletra, unstructured data solutions, data protection, GreenLake Flex and related software. The segment is benefiting from growing demand for AI-ready servers and enterprise infrastructure. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Cloud & AI generated $9.04 billion in revenues, up 25.4% year over year.

HPE's networking develops and sells network and security products and services across campus, branch, data center, routing and security markets. Its portfolio includes wireless access points, switches, routers, gateways, network-management software, support and professional services. The acquisition of Juniper Networks has expanded HPE's networking capabilities and exposure to AI data center infrastructure. HPE's networking revenues reached $2.89 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, rising 10% on a normalized basis.

Corporate Investments and Other includes Advisory and Professional Services, Telco, Instant On and Hewlett Packard Labs. These activities complement HPE's broader technology portfolio through consulting, specialized connectivity offerings and research. Across these businesses, HPE is also expanding GreenLake, its consumption-based hybrid cloud platform, connecting infrastructure, software and services. Together, its three segments position HPE to address demand for AI infrastructure, modern networking and hybrid cloud environments.

Story Continues

HPE Wins Against Competitors With Diverse Portfolio

HPE competes with Super Micro Computer SMCI, Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO in the AI infrastructure market. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers while giving it an edge over its competitors. Super Micro Computer is on track to scale rack production capacity to more than 6,000 AI racks per month by the end of fiscal 2026, including 3,000 direct liquid cooling racks monthly.

Super Micro Computer is already shipping 150kW AI racks in volume and preparing 250kW and 500kW rack solutions to support future high-density AI training and inference workloads. Dell Technologies is a major supplier of servers and storage systems, with a broad customer base across enterprises and cloud providers. Its scale, established distribution and service offerings give it an edge in winning large contracts.

Cisco has also taken $5.3 billion of hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and raised its full-year order outlook to $9 billion from $5 billion. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers. This gives HPE an edge over its competitors.

HPE is also able to keep its margin stable. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HPE's fiscal 2026 margin reflects year-over-year growth of 97%. Estimates have been revised upward over the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Buy HPE Stock Now

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's strong AI infrastructure momentum, expanding AI backlog, growing GreenLake adoption and integrated portfolio support its growth outlook. Despite a sharp share price rally, HPE's valuation remains attractive relative to industry peers. Given these factors, it's prudent to accumulate this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock at present. news.Title: TLS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Identity Strength, Guidance Raised
news.Content:
Telos Corporation TLS reported adjusted earnings of 9 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, unchanged year over year. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 125%, helped by stronger-than-expected performance in its Telos ID business.

Revenues rose 7.3% to $55.2 million, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.4%. Security Solutions growth drove the increase, while the company's Information Assurance business secured more than $58 million in new Xacta and professional services orders.

TLS Rides Security Solutions Growth

Security Solutions revenues climbed 16.6% year over year to $54.18 million from $46.48 million. Expansion of large programs in the Telos ID portfolio led the improvement, with TSA PreCheck enrollment volumes also exceeding management's earlier expectations.

Secure Networks revenues declined 79.6% to $1.01 million from $4.97 million as programs reached completion. Security Solutions accounted for approximately 98% of quarterly revenues compared with roughly 90% in the year-ago period.

Telos Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Telos Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Telos Corporation Quote

Telos Extends Xacta's Reach Across Agencies

New Information Assurance awards span Xacta products and professional services. Management expects the recently secured business to generate approximately $6 million in 2026 revenues and $20 million in 2027, with the contracts characterized as recurring rather than one-time projects.

The company's Xacta 360, Xacta.io and Xacta.ai offerings address security compliance, continuous monitoring and AI-driven automation. Recent engagements extend across defense, intelligence and civilian agencies, while management said previously discussed pending proposals remain separate opportunities.

Telos Brings Higher Profit in Q3 2026

TLS' non-GAAP cash gross profit rose 3.1% to $23.76 million, although cash gross margin contracted to 43.1% from 44.8%. Both margins exceeded management's quarterly expectations.

TLS' adjusted EBITDA grew 4.7% to $10.57 million from $10.10 million, exceeding management's guidance of $6-$6.8 million. This represented the highest quarterly adjusted EBITDA since the company's 2020 IPO. Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 19.2% from 19.6%, despite the stronger dollar profit.

Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses increased 1.8% to $14.03 million. GAAP operating income reached $4.09 million against a loss of $2.47 million a year earlier.

TLS Maintains Robust Cash Conversion

Operating cash flow grew 3.3% to $9.44 million from $9.15 million. Free cash flow increased 11.9% to $7.39 million from $6.60 million, lifting the free cash flow margin to 13.4% from 12.8%. This marked the seventh consecutive quarter above a 12% free cash flow margin.

Story Continues

Telos ended September with $51.76 million in cash and cash equivalents compared with $53.18 million at 2025-end. The company spent $5.7 million to repurchase more than 1.2 million shares during the quarter, bringing year-to-date repurchases to approximately 2.8 million shares for $12.6 million.

Telos Sees Q4 Growth

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Telos expects revenues of $47.5-$50 million, implying 2-7% year-over-year growth. Management expects Information Assurance wins to support sales, with the non-GAAP cash gross margin projected at 43-44.5% on a more favorable mix.

Adjusted EBITDA is forecast at $7-$8.8 million, representing margins of 14.7-17.6%. Adjusted operating expenses are expected to increase approximately $1.2 million year over year, mainly because of higher labor and marketing spending.

TLS Raises 2026 Targets Amid 2027 Transition

Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $198.2-$200.7 million from $187-$195 million, implying 20-22% growth. It also lifted adjusted EBITDA guidance to $32.3-$34.1 million from $23.6-$28.6 million, targeting a margin of 16.3-17%.

Looking ahead, Telos expects the phaseout of low-margin third-party software resale to create a $32 million revenue headwind in 2027, with a modest profit impact. Management estimates the exit could improve gross margin by approximately 600 basis points on a full-year run-rate basis. It also expects a 400-basis-point sequential margin improvement from TSA PreCheck in the second half of 2027.

TLS' Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

TLS currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

news.Title: Will Semtech's SGP.32 eSIM Launch Expand Its Cellular IoT Business?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC is expanding its cellular Internet of Things (IoT) portfolio with the launch of SGP.32 multi-profile eSIM under its Smart Connectivity Premium offering. The new solution allows customers to use a single SIM SKU with multiple mobile network operator profiles across different regions. Managed through Semtech's AirVantage eSIM platform, the offering is designed to simplify connectivity for businesses deploying IoT devices globally. It also addresses challenges such as dependence on a single carrier, permanent roaming restrictions and the need to replace SIM cards when network providers change.

The new offering is based on the GSMA's SGP.32 standard, which supports remote provisioning and management of eSIM profiles. Through AirVantage, customers can add local carrier profiles, manage subscriptions and switch between networks without physically replacing SIM cards. The platform also supports bulk provisioning and allows businesses to connect their own systems through application programming interfaces. This gives customers greater flexibility in managing large IoT deployments across different countries and networks.

Semtech's solution can serve several IoT applications. Fixed devices, such as smart meters and video surveillance systems, can use multiple carrier profiles to address roaming restrictions and maintain connectivity through network failover. Mobile assets can also benefit from access to different carriers across regions, improving network coverage and reliability. Semtech is also offering a PowerSave eSIM designed for battery-powered devices. It uses a dual-profile setup to optimize network connection time and support the transfer of critical data while preserving battery life.

The GSMA's SGP.32 standard is expected to make adoption easier by simplifying remote provisioning and profile management. As global IoT deployments expand, Smart Connectivity Premium could help Semtech attract more enterprise customers seeking flexible, reliable and easier-to-manage connectivity solutions and strengthen its position in cellular IoT connectivity. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 46.2% and 33.8%, respectively.

How Competitors Fare Against SMTC

Semtech faces competition from Digi International DGII and Cisco Systems CSCO in the global IoT connectivity market.

Digi International offers SGP.32-compatible eSIMs that support remote carrier switching and profile management through its Digi Remote Manager platform. This allows customers to manage connectivity across distributed IoT devices without physically replacing SIM cards. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported record revenues of $139 million, up 29% year over year. DIGI attributed its growth to contributions across products, services and solutions, supported by higher product volumes and strong customer demand. Its remote management capabilities and focus on connected devices strengthen its position in the IoT connectivity market.

Story Continues

Cisco Systems offers an eSIM Orchestrator through its IoT Control Center, which supports the SGP.32 standard and enables customers to remotely download, activate and manage eSIM profiles in bulk. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, orders for its industrial IoT portfolio grew at a double-digit rate for the ninth consecutive quarter, driven by deployments in manufacturing, utilities and data center facilities. CSCO's broader IoT and networking portfolio, combined with its eSIM orchestration capabilities, gives it an opportunity to serve businesses looking to manage connected devices across multiple locations.

SMTC's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of SMTC have jumped 58% in the year-to-date period compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's return of 25.3%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

news.Content:

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of -39.39%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post a loss of $0.35 per share when it actually produced a loss of $0.37, delivering a surprise of -5.71%.

This compares to year-ago revenues of $169.71 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

What's Next for BITDEER TEC GRP?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for BITDEER TEC GRP was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Story Continues

Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

依盤勢來看，創業板指領漲，市場風格偏向高彈性方向，儘管盤中漲幅一度收斂，但收盤仍維持優勢，反映資金對成長與題材族群的偏好較為明顯。成交量方面，滬市今日成交6,740億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交8,309億元，兩市成交額1兆5,049億元，較前一交易日量增約2%。

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉中國貿易順差突破1兆美元 三大指數走高
news.Content:
中國股市A股三大指數周二（10日）收盤走高，最新數據顯示，中國10月進口創下2021年以來最大增幅，且出口連續第二個月成長超過 35%，中國今年來貿易順差迅速膨脹至突破1兆美元。

上證指數周二收報3,663.72點，漲0.08%。深證成指收報11,241.54點，漲0.86%。創業板指收報2,494.40點，漲1.46%。

中國海關總署周二公布的數據顯示，上月進口增幅遠超預期，較去年同期激增近42%。出口則成長 35.2%，10月貿易順差為1,053 億美元，是5月以來最少。

國泰君安國際控股公司首席經濟學家周浩（Hao Zhou）表示，貿易順差凸顯即便中國面對全球貿易環境日益嚴峻的挑戰，出口產業依然具備韌性與競爭力。

儘管中國與歐盟的緊張關係加劇，且美國等其他主要市場採取保護主義措施，中國今年商品貿易順差仍再次突破1兆美元。去年中國貿易順差寫下1.2兆美元歷史新高。

今年前 10 個月，中國的貿易順差比去年同期成長近 9%。

今年出口大幅成長，主要歸功於全球對人工智慧（AI）硬體的需求暴增，這類產品在全亞洲的貿易往來也十分熱絡。雖然中國的進口也有所成長，但仍落後於出口，且增幅主要侷限於黃金等少數特定商品，顯示內需依然缺乏明顯復甦跡象。

不過，中國出口強勁勢頭並不限於AI 硬體。高盛集團的分析顯示，若從出口數量來看，成長動能來自廣泛高科技產品，從中共高層推廣的「新三樣」產業——太陽能、電動車與鋰電池——到工業機器人皆包含在內。

news.Title: AI晶片股回神！韓日領軍反彈、台股祭限空令終結連七跌 市場緊盯CPI
news.Content:
亞洲股市周二(10日)延續全球科技股強勁反彈走勢，南韓與日本股市領漲，台股終結連七日跌勢。但由於輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳相關風波未明朗，加上美國通膨報告即將公布，投資人對這波反彈能否續航仍抱持審慎態度。

在華爾街創下約七個月來最大單日漲幅後，投資人正在重新買進先前遭重挫的晶片股。美國總統川普則釋出訊號，若與伊朗談判取得進展，美國不太可能再度發動攻擊，帶動油價進一步回落，緩解通膨疑慮也提振市場情緒。

MSCI亞太指數盤中上漲2%，南韓KOSPI指數大漲逾4%，日本日經225指數上漲超過2%，東證股價指數(TOPIX)上漲2.2%。

亞洲交易時段，那斯達克100期貨微跌不到0.1%，標普500期貨小漲0.15%。

韓股部分，SK海力士股價上漲6.3%，三星電子上漲4.9%。日股方面，鎧俠(Kioxia)上漲6.6%，TDK上漲5.2%，村田製作所上漲5.9%，LG Innotek上漲5.1%。

台灣加權指數盤中漲幅一度達6.4%，終場漲幅仍有2.5%。台積電(2330-TW)上漲2.2%，大立光(3008-TW)上漲2.8%，鴻海(2317-TW)上漲2.5%。

台股到周一為止已連七日下跌，創2022年以來最長連跌紀錄，周二終於止跌反彈。台灣金管會將放空額度上限從原本前30日平均成交量的30%調降至3%，並將最低融資保證金成數從90%提高至130%，同時維持最高新台幣5000億元(約152億美元)穩定市場基金可供運用。

日本與台灣股市上周均進入熊市，南韓股市則較夏季高點下跌逾40%，三星電子與SK海力士股價一度累計下跌逾16%。

美國10月消費者物價指數(CPI)將於周二公布，市場預期整體CPI與核心CPI將分別月增0.3%及0.2%。目前市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期機率已從一周前的74%升至84%。

另外，Anthropic周二可能展開的首次公開發行(IPO)投資人說明會，上市計畫，尋求最高693億美元估值，Anthropic上市計畫與本周稍晚的與CoreWeave(CRWV-US)財報，將成為觀察AI投資人意願的重要指標。

news.Title: 不演了？ 台股漲幅大收斂 他追旺宏、華邦電秒被套
news.Content:
台股今（10）日早盤跳空開高，盤中一度大漲逾1400點，不過隨著時間推移，漲勢一度逐漸收斂近千點，所幸在台積電由黑翻紅，也日月光、南亞、台達電重新鎖回漲停下，成功守住42000點大關。

台股上周歷經重挫回檔，指數一度摜破38000點，周一則迎來報復性反彈，今日則延續漲勢，早盤一度大漲逾1400點，雖然衝上43135點高點後一路下滑，漲勢收斂逾千點，但在觸及41930點後，在權值股集體拉抬下，指數又再度上揚400點，於42300點附近震盪；截至上午11:55點暫報42312點，上漲654點，漲幅1.57%。

權值股部分，台積電開高震盪，早盤衝上2280元後震盪走低，盤中甚至一度翻黑，但隨即又迅速翻紅成功，小漲5元，暫報2240元；台達電、南亞、日月光等權值股在大筆賣單下也一度漲停打開，不過後續又成功亮燈漲停。

針對今日的盤勢，有股民在臉書社團「當沖勒戒所」發文分享，早上看大漲於是衝進去買旺宏、華邦電，沒想到漲勢收斂，現賣現套「今天早上進場買旺宏、華邦電，馬上賠錢。」

留言區網友紛紛安慰，「平常心吧！很多人成交後，眼睜睜看著股價開始往下掉，笑你的人也發生過啦！」、「沒事的 當沖華邦電現在懊悔中」、「我買0050都能大賠了」；也有網友表示，「追高殺低才是真散戶」、「韭韭的」、「韭菜來了」。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 台積電營收出爐前...股價漲45元「市值重返59兆元大關」 1天增加一家南亞科
news.Content:
台積電（2330）10月營收於今（10）日下午出爐！在市場買盤與卡位資金強勢湧入下，台積電今日盤中強勢衝上 2,280元，上漲45元，漲幅超過2%，伴隨股價走揚，台積電整體市值也從 57.95 兆元直接衝上 59.11 兆元大關，光是單日市值就狂增逾1兆元，相當於一天拉出一整家南亞科的總市值，使市值重新站穩59兆元整數關卡。

資深台股分析師蔡明翰表示，輝達執行長黃仁勳陷入桃色風波，昨日輝達（Nvidia）釋出負面訊息引發修正，台積電今早表現卻展現極強韌性，雖然輝達與台積電連動度極高，致使昨日台積電 ADR 表現相對費城半導體指數略顯疲弱，但關鍵在於「該利空並未在整體半導體族群中擴散」，且費半指數終場仍強勢大漲。

蔡明翰指出，輝達昨日開低後並未一路下殺，反而出現強烈的開低拉回支撐，顯示市場對於10月至11月這波AI 族群大幅修正的「利空已出現鈍化現象」。當市場對利空不再過度恐慌，代表股市底部位階已經逐步確認，資金自然會重新回流核心績優股。因此只要輝達沒有發生實質性產業風暴，情緒未進一步惡化，這波大幅修正期已告一段落，對台股與台積電後市絕對是正面利多。

針對投資人的後續操作策略，蔡明翰提出兩大核心觀察點，第一，利空不跌即是底：市場目前已不再將輝達個案消息視為無差別利空解讀，AI 供應鏈最壞情況漸過，投資人毋須過度恐慌；第二，留意本周美股 CoreWeave 財報：身為 AI 算力基礎設施指標的 CoreWeave 即將公布財報，市場普遍預期其本業仍處虧損且資本支出龐大，若財報公布後市場能以「利空出盡」或理性態度消化，將進一步奠定AI族群築底反彈的堅實基礎。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: KOSPI早盤大漲5.1%，韓交所啟動買方Sidecar
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】韓國股市週二(10日)早盤強勁反彈，韓國綜合股價指數(KOSPI)漲幅擴大至5.1%，報5,276.81點，站上5,200點。韓國交易所隨即啟動買方Sidecar，暫停程式交易買單。買方Sidecar是韓股期貨急漲時啟動的交易措施，暫停範圍限於程式交易買單，其他交易仍可進行。

隔夜美股科技股走強，那指收漲2.74%，費城半導體指數大漲6.85%，為亞洲科技股早盤反彈提供助力。費半上週重挫逾12%，週一由超微與博通帶動回升。

韓股上週曾因AI投資前景疑慮遭遇賣壓，半導體權值股首當其衝。週二大盤急彈後，三星電子與SK海力士能否延續反彈，仍是觀察韓股漲勢的重點。

news.Title: Will Cisco Systems (CSCO) Deliver the Strong Results the Market Needs to See?
news.Content:
With technology stocks recently coming under pressure amid concerns about lofty AI valuations, potential regulatory scrutiny, and immense infrastructure spending, Cisco Systems CSCO) will be among the most important AI-related companies reporting earnings this week.

While CSCO has not escaped the recent selloff, its strong year-to-date performance underscores investors' renewed enthusiasm for established networking and hardware companies.

Cisco's success highlights how the AI infrastructure buildout has revitalized longstanding technology leaders, including Dell Technologies DELL) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE), whose networking, servers, and computing hardware have become increasingly critical to AI data centers.

With Cisco scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter results after market hours on Thursday, November 12, expectations are high for another strong quarter.

Cisco's Q1 Expectations

Cisco is expected to report Q1 adjusted earnings of $1.33 per share, representing 33% year-over-year growth from EPS of $1.00 in the prior-year quarter. This comes as Q1 revenue is projected to increase nearly 22% to $18.09 billion from $14.88 billion a year ago.

Momentum has been impressive, with Cisco's fiscal Q4 revenue rising 18% to $17.25 billion and adjusted EPS jumping 23% to $1.22.

More importantly, Cisco is benefiting from accelerating demand for AI networking infrastructure. The company secured $9.3 billion in AI infrastructure orders during fiscal 2026 and expects AI-related revenue from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in its current FY27, up from approximately $4 billion last year.

Investors will be closely watching whether this momentum can support another guidance increase, particularly as growing sales of lower-margin AI networking hardware could pressure overall gross margins.

CSCO Performance & Valuation Comparison

Despite the recent tech selloff, Cisco stock has still gained nearly 30% YTD, comfortably outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq's returns of just under 10%.

Over the last three years, CSCO has delivered a total return of more than 100% when including dividends, compared with roughly 80% for the broader indexes.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

At current levels of just under $100 a share, CSCO trades at 20X forward earnings, which is roughly on par with its Zacks Computer-Networking Industry average and near the S&P 500's 18X.

This suggests investors aren't paying an excessive premium for Cisco's expanding AI exposure, although its valuation is no longer as inexpensive as it was before the AI infrastructure spending boom. While CSCO trades above its decade-long median of 16X forward earnings, shares are still more than 35% below a high of 32X during this period.

Story Continues

Cisco's Generous Dividend

Intriguingly, Cisco offers a compelling income opportunity that remains relatively uncommon among major AI infrastructure beneficiaries and many tech stocks in general.

Its quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share equates to an annual payout of $1.68 and a yield approaching 2%, providing additional appeal for long-term investors.

Bottom Line: Can Cisco Keep Its Momentum?

Sporting a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , Cisco Systems remains an attractive way to capitalize on the AI infrastructure buildout without paying the premium valuations often associated with semiconductor and software stocks.

Strong quarterly results and upbeat guidance could reinforce confidence in Cisco's AI-driven growth trajectory while providing much-needed reassurance to investors following the broader tech selloff. However, sustained revenue growth and healthy margins will be essential to maintaining the stock's resilient momentum.

news.Title: Brave’s Leo assistant uses NEAR AI to prove its AI chats stay private, paving the way for businesses to use AI with sensitive data
news.Content:
Most of the AI tools businesses have adopted so far handle low-risk work, such as drafting emails, summarizing calls and cleaning up slide decks.

The material companies would most like to hand over is the material they guard most closely.

That includes financial research before it's published, legal files covered by attorney-client privilege and internal data on pricing, products and deals.

What holds that work back is usually not what the models can do. It's what happens to the data once it leaves the building.

Sending a confidential document to an AI model means trusting the cloud provider, the chip operator and the AI company not to see it. Most of the time, that trust rests on a privacy policy.

Related: Bernie Sanders spots opportunity as 66% of Americans oppose AI data centers

The pressure is showing up in corporate budgets. In Cisco's 2026 Data and Privacy Benchmark Study , 90% of the more than 5,200 IT and security professionals surveyed said their privacy programs have expanded because of AI. Cisco puts it plainly:

"AI ambition is outpacing readiness."

The cost of getting it wrong is rising too. IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report puts the average breach at $4.99 million, a record. Attacks that pull sensitive data back out of AI models cost even more, at $6 million on average.

NEAR AI , the AI arm of the NEAR ecosystem, is building its business around replacing that policy with proof.

On October 15, the company announced that Leo, the AI assistant built into the Brave browser, now runs on private inference from NEAR AI Cloud.

Inference is the step where a model reads a prompt and produces an answer, and it's where user data is most exposed.

A locked room the operator can't enter

According to NEAR AI, Leo conversations on the GLM 5.3 Flash model run inside trusted execution environments, or TEEs.

A TEE is a walled-off section of a processor where code and data are shielded from the rest of the machine. NEAR AI says its TEEs are built on Intel TDX and NVIDIA Confidential Compute.

The company says the cloud host, the GPU operator and NEAR AI itself are "cryptographically locked out." Leo encrypts each prompt in the browser with a protocol called Oblivious HTTP, using a key that exists only inside the enclave.

Brave's relay strips the user's IP address before passing the request on. NEAR AI says memory stays encrypted while the model runs, and every response is signed inside the enclave.

The bigger point is who does the checking. Before Leo receives the enclave's key, Brave's own open-source verifier checks the hardware against Intel's signature and NVIDIA 's attestation service.

Story Continues

Attestation is a cryptographic proof of what hardware and software are running.

The verifier also rebuilds NEAR AI's code from public source to confirm it matches what is deployed. As the post puts it: "No pass, no key."

NEAR AI's Trust Center puts it in business terms. It says privacy is "enforced by hardware, not policy," and verifiable through attestation "checked against Intel and NVIDIA, not NEAR AI."

Trending on TheStreet Roundtable:

Veteran economist says investors are watching the wrong bubble

Billionaire Ray Dalio sounds alarm on AI's $4.4 trillion debt squeeze

Two big U.S.-listed Bitcoin miners plan major exit for AI

Brave's reach as a distribution channel

Distribution may matter as much as the technology. Privacy tools usually struggle because users have to go find them. Inside a browser, private inference becomes a setting.

Brave currently serves over 130 million monthly active users . That figure shows the size of the potential audience.

Private inference applies only to Brave Leo users who choose GLM 5.3 Flash in the model settings.

The rollout came in stages. Brave began testing NEAR AI's TEEs in November 2025 with DeepSeek V3.1 in Brave Nightly, its experimental build. The October release takes it to the full production browser.

Brendan Eich, co-founder and CEO of Brave, called the integration "a first for AI chats in browsers." Illia Polosukhin, co-founder of NEAR, framed it as a question of ownership.

"Browsers are a primary computing interface that handles all of our personal information, so it's critical that AI is introduced in a user-owned way," Polosukhin said.

NEAR AI says Brave joins Venice AI, Abound and the Government of Bermuda among organizations running production workloads on NEAR AI Cloud.

That mix of consumer apps and a public-sector user hints at the same distribution model at work: privacy delivered through software people already use, rather than a standalone product.

Guarantees that stop at the model

For businesses weighing sensitive workloads, the fine print matters. The privacy guarantee in the

Brave announcement covers one model in one deployment. NEAR AI describes GLM 5.3 Flash as an open-weights model under the MIT license, meaning its underlying parameters are public.

NEAR AI's Trust Center specifies that open-weight models hosted by NEAR AI run inside the TEEs. Third-party models are also offered, but NEAR AI says those are "proxied without revealing the customer's identity and processed under the provider's own data terms."

In other words, the hardware guarantee applies only where NEAR AI controls the hardware.

That distinction will likely shape how companies buy. A guarantee tied to a named model, a named deployment and an attestation anyone can check gives them something to audit.

NEAR AI also says a hardware-attested deployment log confirms that the model a user picks is the one answering.

Publishing open-source verification and relying on chipmakers' attestation services rather than its own word lets NEAR AI's approach be tested from outside.

For businesses that have kept their most sensitive files away from AI, that offers a way to bring them in without taking anyone's word for it.

Related: $13 trillion brokerage giant offers cheapest ways to trade crypto

news.Title: Cisco Q1 Earnings – Here’s What Analysts Expect from CSCO Stock amid AI Trade Concerns
news.Content:
Networking giant Cisco Systems (CSCO) will announce its fiscal first-quarter earnings on November 12. While CSCO stock has declined 20% over the past month amid AI trade concerns and broader market pressures, it is still up 22% year-to-date. Cisco bulls remain optimistic due to AI-led demand for its products, with the company guiding for AI infrastructure revenue of $7.5 billion in FY27, up from $4 billion in the previous year. However, some analysts remain cautious about margins and contend that the demand optimism is already priced into the stock.

Wall Street expects Cisco to report Q1 FY27 EPS (earnings per share) of $1.32 , up 32% from the prior-year quarter. Revenue is projected to rise about 22% to $18.11 billion. Investors will focus on the momentum in AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers. A potential slowdown could weigh on CSCO stock.

Analysts' Views Ahead of CSCO's Q1 Earnings

Last week, Morgan Stanley analyst Meta Marshall downgraded her rating on Cisco stock to Hold from Buy and lowered her price target to $120 from $135.
